questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the host university had interesting courses and a good study environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, seeing that the UCD Erasmus office and UCD in general provide good resources for informing the students of things and dates to be aware of.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance in form of guidance from the Erasmus team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found accomodation on an online platform called HostingPower and I had a good experience renting a room through this website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should be aware of public transport and how especially the busses can be a litlle unreliable at times - especially during rushhour.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: By following UCD's padlet for exchange students, it was very easy registrating for courses and subsequently getting access to the university's online platform where an email account was set up for us, where we would recieve further information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are many helpful resources at UCD, such as, health care services, academic writing workshops, the student desk, the Erasmus office etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found the process of registrating for courses easy and if a course had already allocated all its spots, then it was easy finding a similar course to registrer for instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For future exchange students, I would recommend to have a few other courses in mind other than the main courses you wish to get, since it can be a reality that some of the courses get filled very quickly and then you need to apply for other courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 6 courses on level 1-3 and found the workload with test, assignments, mid-terms and the exams to be accomplishable while still having a social life and time for other things besides studying.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching is quite similar between UCPH and UCD, since they both operate with lectures and tutorials/seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was enrolled in the courses called: Sociology of Crime and Deviance, Critical Thinking, Introduction to Ethics, Introduction to Irish studies, Lost Cities & Writing Dublin.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend future students to take the course Critical Thinking as it requires you to think differently and more thoroughly with an aim to develop a better analytical way of reasoning.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I would say that the most unexpected cost before beginning my exchange period was the cost of housing as this is very expensive in general in Dublin. Otherwise, I did not really encouter an unexpected cost during my stay.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transport is very cheap and especially being a student it only costs 1 euro per bus ride.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a large variety of societies and clubs for students at UCD. All from draw society, international student society, mature society, film society, athletics club etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think most people would appreciate film society, since it is a nice way to unwind after being in academic settings throughout the day.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I think exchange students should go to the city centre as it is a bus ride on 15-20 minutes away from UCD, and here plenty of free admission museums are available for people to visit. Moreover, UCD plans several trips throughout the semester for students to go to other locations in Ireland with beautiful nature sites and historical sites.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think the Erasmus team did a great job doing a lot of activities and events for exchange students to get to know each other. And in general the students at the university are very friendly and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The best way to socialise with local students would be to join societies and clubs or to talk to students in tutotials or before and after lectures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the Irish culture is a very open and accepting culture which results in a great diversity both on campus but also in the city centre. Therefore, I did not find it difficult to enjoy the culture and speak with the Irish people around me.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate how visible the Irish history is in their land- and cityscape with their many churces and beautiful ancient architecture. Furthermore, their music, food, pubs and sports are all great cultural things to engage in as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Search for accomodation early in the process, since it can be very difficult to find affordable accomodation in Dublin.
2. Ask for help if you need help with anything, since the teachers and the Erasmus team are all very helpful and happy to help you out.   
3. Push yourself to talk to people in your courses even though it might seem a little intimidating to begin with, because it is great having people to talk to about course related stuff but also for the benefit of social plans in non-academic settings.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It might also be useful to remeber that it is a very big university. So, if you need to study and if you want to preferably sit in a librabry, there are a couple to choose from. The James Joyce library is great, but it can get a little packed there, so remeber to investigate the rest of campus and the other buildings where good study spots are located as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was very rewarding having a great dialogue with the teachers and having good tutorials where you could see your own progress. It was also great getting to know so many very nice students on campus.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was finding affordable accommodation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
